title: From Zero to Mega-Gauss Fields: Comprehensive Magnetophotonic Spectroscopy of Graphene Dirac Cones
abstract: We investigate the infrared magneto-optical response of n-doped epitaxial graphene on 4H-SiC in ultrahigh magnetic fields up to 560~T, utilizing single-turn coil and electromagnetic flux compression techniques. The measured absorption spectra are anomalously broad, strongly deviating from conventional cyclotron resonance. Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) reveals a distorted Dirac dispersion featuring a ``camel-back" structure with an energy gap of $E_g \sim 0.2$~eV. Using the band parameters extracted via a generalized bilayer graphene model, we construct a Landau level (LL) fan chart that dictates a critical level crossing between the $N=0^+$ and $N=0^-$ states near 160--200~T. At this threshold, the optical transition mechanism undergoes a dramatic shift from an electron-dominated collective mode to a cooperative electron-hole collective excitation. Furthermore, the extreme-field absorption spectra under thulium fiber laser excitation ($\hbarω_0 = 0.636$~eV)---culminating in a massive resonance near 400~T with a shoulder at 200~T---are excellently reproduced by a collective Alfvén wave model. This analysis also evidences a magnetic-field-induced enhancement of the sublattice potential asymmetry parameter (from 0.10~eV to 0.12~eV). This directly signifies that the macroscopic electron-hole band asymmetry is further amplified by the applied magnetic field. Ultimately, the field-induced energy inversion generates a strongly interacting, fully compensated electron-hole plasma. The resonant excitation of Alfvén waves in this regime demonstrates that a pristine tabletop analog to the relativistic electron-positron plasmas found in astrophysical extremes can be elegantly realized within a 2D graphene system.
summary: The authors studied graphene's optical response in ultrahigh magnetic fields, finding that the behavior deviates significantly from simple models. They demonstrated that at extreme fields, the system forms a fully compensated electron-hole plasma whose collective excitations are accurately described by an Alfvén wave model. This work establishes graphene as a platform for simulating astrophysical relativistic plasmas.
main_problem: To investigate the infrared magneto-optical response of n-doped epitaxial graphene under ultrahigh magnetic fields, specifically determining if the system deviates from ideal Dirac cone behavior.
main_result: The extreme-field absorption spectra are excellently reproduced by a collective Alfvén wave model, demonstrating that the 2D graphene system can realize a tabletop analog to relativistic electron-positron plasmas.
method: A combination of experimental magneto-optical spectroscopy (using single-turn coils and flux compression) and theoretical modeling based on generalized bilayer graphene Hamiltonians was employed.
model_or_system: The physical system is n-doped epitaxial graphene on 4H-SiC, modeled using effective Hamiltonians that account for band warping and electron-hole plasma dynamics in extreme magnetic fields. The analysis transitions from single-particle cyclotron resonance to collective Alfvén wave excitations.
key_observables: Anomalously broad magneto-absorption spectra, 'camel-back' structure in ARPES dispersion, critical level crossing between $N=0^+$ and $N=0^-$ Landau levels.
important_parameters: Magnetic field up to 560 T; energy gap $E_g \sim 0.2$ eV; magnetic enhancement of sublattice potential asymmetry (0.10 eV to 0.12 eV).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the high-field behavior is governed by collective plasma modes rather than single-particle cyclotron resonance, necessitating the use of a bilayer-derived model for LL calculations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows magneto-transmission spectra using various lasers; Figure 2 displays ARPES data showing the 'camel-back' structure; and Figure 3 illustrates calculated Landau Level fan charts predicting level crossing near 160–200 T.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first observing anomalous optical responses, then using ARPES to map a distorted Dirac dispersion, theoretically modeling the high-field LL behavior showing a critical crossover, and finally interpreting the extreme-field spectra via the collective Alfvén wave model.
why_interesting: This work bridges condensed matter physics (graphene) with high-energy astrophysics concepts (relativistic plasma), using advanced magneto-optics to probe fundamental quantum electrodynamic effects in a solid-state system.

The center of the energy gap (the yellow dashed line) is positioned approximately 0.18 eV below the Fermi energy (EF ), indicated by the sky blue dashed line.
